q: In a metallic bond, the valence electrons of the atoms are very loosely held, forming a common _____ cloud.
e: In a metallic bond, the valence electrons of the atoms are very loosely held, forming a common electron cloud. Valence electrons sit in the outermost shell, and those are the electrons that actually form bonds.

q: These mobile electrons in metallic bonding are often described as a "sea of _____".
e: These mobile electrons in metallic bonding are often described as a "sea of electrons". Metallic bonding is the attraction between metal cations and a sea of delocalised electrons.

q: The positively charged metallic nuclei are surrounded by _____ electrons.
e: The positively charged metallic nuclei are surrounded by free-moving electrons. Free-moving: metallic bonding is metal cations in a sea of delocalised electrons.

q: Metals consist of giant structures of atoms that are packed closely together in a regular arrangement called a _____.
e: Metals consist of giant structures of atoms that are packed closely together in a regular arrangement called a lattice. A crystal lattice is the repeating 3D pattern of particles in a solid.

q: The strength of metallic bonding increases with the increasing positive charge on the ions in the metal _____.
e: The strength of metallic bonding increases with the increasing positive charge on the ions in the metal lattice. Metallic bonding is the attraction between metal cations and a sea of delocalised electrons.

q: The strength of metallic bonding increases with the _____ size of metal ions in the lattice.
e: The strength of metallic bonding increases with the decreasing size of metal ions in the lattice. Metallic bonding is the attraction between metal cations and a sea of delocalised electrons.

q: The strength of metallic bonding increases with the increasing number of _____ electrons per atom.
e: The strength of metallic bonding increases with the increasing number of mobile electrons per atom. Core electrons stay inner and do not bond.

q: The strength of metallic bond is _____ than that of an ionic bond.
e: The strength of metallic bond is lower than that of an ionic bond. Metallic bonding is the attraction between metal cations and a sea of delocalised electrons.

q: Consequently, the melting points of some metals become _____ compared with the ionic compounds.
e: Consequently, the melting points of some metals become lower compared with the ionic compounds. Ionic bonding is electron transfer followed by the pull between opposite ions.

q: The bonding in metals results from the interaction of the mobile electrons with the various nuclei, hence they are held together by a strong _____ attraction.
e: The bonding in metals results from the interaction of the mobile electrons with the various nuclei, hence they are held together by a strong electrostatic attraction. An ether has an oxygen between two carbon groups, C-O-C.
